summary: Dedicated pool throughput erosion correlated with background prefetch churn and GPU banking events
description: Issue summary: Customer DataLoom reports graduated throughput erosion in their dedicated GPU pool starting 2026-03-12 08:30 UTC. The customer sees normal request rates but a steady rise in p95/p99 latency and reduced throughput despite autoscaler not scaling up. Impact: Several production routes backed by dedicated pool show 30-60% throughput loss at peak; customer-facing inference degraded and some requests time out. Environment: Dedicated pool (reserved) in us-east running mixed rw-7b-v2 and redwood-open-13b workloads with KV-prefetch enabled. Steps to reproduce: 1) Route steady load to dedicated pool with mixed short/long streams. 2) Observe allocator metrics and batcher utilization. 3) Note prefetch eviction/renewal spikes correlated with GPU banking churn. Observed behavior: - Gradual p95 increase from 150ms -> 650ms over ~90 minutes. - Autoscaler remains at same GPU count; allocation attach rate drops intermittently. - Metrics show frequent prefetch lease churn (prefetch-lease-renew spikes) and repeated GPU bank reassignments. - Logs include allocator warnings: "banking_reassign_timeout" and sidecar messages about heavy nvlink IO backpressure. Expected behavior: Stable throughput with autoscaler increasing capacity or scheduler balancing to maintain p95. Initial hypothesis: A background prefetcher process combined with uneven GPU banking (banking here refers to the driver-level memory bank affinity) is causing repeated small KV-cache evictions and brief GPU attach contention which the autoscaler telemetry misses because attach failures are short-lived. This looks like a noisy-tenant effect where many small prefetches from one customer/process cause I/O bursts and GPU bank thrash, reducing effective batch formation and starving some inference lanes. Evidence/Logs: - Grafana panels: allocator/attach_rate, prefetch/lease_renew_count, gpu/bank_reassigns (links in comments). - Sidecar logs show repeated "prefetch: evicted 512 entries" lines around times of throughput drops. - SRE sampling: top IO processes on GPU host show snapshot-writer and background-health-checker with spikes. Short-term mitigation applied: routed customer TrafficGroup A to alternate dedicated pool (fallback) at 2026-03-12T10:05Z which restored baseline throughput for critical routes. Long-term next steps: deeper kernel/driver trace of banking reassigns, correlate with NVMe/NVLink IO metrics, add autoscaler instrumentation to detect attach-failure-frequency as a signal for proactive scale-up, consider limiting prefetch parallelism per tenant. Attachments: links to Grafana snapshots and S3 logs in comments.
comments: 2026-03-12T09:10:00Z - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer reports throughput drift and p99 spikes. Collected initial traces and asked for host IDs. Asked SRE to triage gpu attach logs.

2026-03-12T09:50:00Z - SRE (Diego Morales): Observed repeated 'banking_reassign_timeout' in allocator logs on hosts gpu-us-east-3b-0[12]. Prefetch lease_renew_count up 8x versus baseline. Hypothesis: background prefetcher creating IO bursts that trigger bank reassigns and short attach retries.

2026-03-12T10:07:00Z - Support (Aisha Patel): Implemented traffic steering to fallback dedicated pool (TrafficGroup A). Customer reports latency normalized on critical routes. Leaving original pool under observation.

2026-03-12T11:22:00Z - Customer (DataLoom - Rajiv Menon): Noted improvement after steering; still seeing intermittent timeouts for long-context streams. Provided request_ids and sample logs to support@redwood.ai.

2026-03-12T13:05:00Z - Runtime Eng (Marta Kim): Added verbose driver-bind debug and requested kernel traces for next repro window. Created GH PR to add attach-failure metric (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842).

2026-03-14T08:30:00Z - SRE (Diego Morales): Correlated NVMe queue depth spikes with prefetch eviction windows. Proposed throttling prefetch parallelism at tenant level and a short-term autoscaler tweak to react on attach-failure-rate. Scheduling follow-up with Scheduling team.

2026-03-14T09:15:00Z - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer notified of ongoing investigation and short-term plan: 1) enable tenant prefetch throttle, 2) instrument attach-failure metric, 3) keep TrafficGroup A on fallback until throttle validated. Awaiting Scheduling and Runtime changes for rollout.
2026-03-14T12:00:00Z - Scheduling (Evan Li): Created internal task INT-221338 to evaluate autoscaler signal adjustment; linking here for tracking.
resolution: Mitigation applied: customer traffic moved to fallback pool to restore service for critical routes. Ongoing remediation: implement tenant prefetch throttle, add attach-failure telemetry to autoscaler, and run driver-level trace. No permanent fix yet; monitoring in place and customer notified of next steps.
